 Search "The Blue Road" Premieres Tonight on Netflix: Son Suk-ku Leads Korea-Japan Crime Thriller
 Disha Paul 50 minutes ago 3 min read Son Suk-ku (left) and Eita Nagayama join forces in The Blue Road , Netflix's new cross-border crime thriller about a chilling series of murders connecting South Korea and Japan. (Netflix) What happens when a Korean detective and a Japanese detective are forced to work together to catch a serial killer? If the trailer for Netflix's upcoming thriller The Blue Road  is anything to go by, things are about to get very messy. 
 Starring Son Suk-ku and Japanese actor Eita Nagayama , the upcoming series combines gruesome murders, international investigations, and a mystery that crosses national borders. Set around the time of the 2002 Korea-Japan FIFA World Cup , the drama also brings an interesting historical backdrop to its crime story. 
 With D.P.  director Han Jun-hee behind the camera, this is one Netflix thriller that deserves a place on your November watchlist. 
 What Is The Blue Road About? 
 The Blue Road  begins with a disturbing discovery in Tokyo. A dead body is found with a Korean message written in blood. Soon, another similarly disturbing murder takes place in South Korea, this time with a Japanese message. 
 The strange similarities lead investigators to suspect that a serial killer is operating across both countries. 
 The Blue Road (Netflix) Son Suk-ku plays Kim Seok, a detective with the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency, while Eita Nagayama plays Inose, a detective from the Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department. The two are brought together to investigate the killings, but their partnership does not begin smoothly. 
 Kim Seok wants to work together, while Inose initially refuses to cooperate, making their already complicated investigation even more difficult. 
 As the murders continue, the detectives encounter dangerous figures, hidden connections, and clues that take the investigation far beyond Seoul and Tokyo. 
 Who Stars in The Blue Road ? 
 The Blue Road (Netflix) The series brings together Korean and Japanese actors, making its international cast one of its biggest attractions. 
 Son Suk-ku as Kim Seok:  A Seoul detective investigating the mysterious murders. 
 Eita Nagayama as Inose:  A Tokyo detective who becomes involved in the cross-border investigation. 
 Kim Shin-rok as Li Yoon-ok:  A Zainichi Korean businesswoman with her own agenda. 
 Jung Jae-young as Seo Hyun-tae:  A powerful figure in Japan's criminal underworld. 
 Choi Sung-eun as Yoon Soo-kyung:  A government agent whose interests bring her into conflict with Inose. 
 The combination of Son Suk-ku and Eita Nagayama is particularly interesting. Rather than following one detective throughout the investigation, the series gives viewers two leads with different backgrounds and approaches to solving crimes. 
 Why Should Thriller Fans Watch The Blue Road? 
 One of the most interesting things about The Blue Road  is its 2002 setting. The story unfolds during the Korea-Japan World Cup, a major sporting event co-hosted by the two countries. 
 This gives the thriller a distinctive backdrop while allowing the investigation to move between different countries and communities. 
 The main trailer also offers glimpses of Central Asian landscapes and Hong Kong's Kowloon Walled City, suggesting that the mystery will eventually become much bigger than a conventional police investigation. 
 Another reason to keep an eye on the series is its director, Han Jun-hee. His previous Netflix work includes D.P. , known for its intense storytelling and grounded approach to difficult subjects. 
 If The Blue Road  can bring the same attention to character development and suspense, it could become an interesting addition to Netflix's Korean thriller lineup. 
 When and Where to Watch The Blue Road 
 The Blue Road  will premiere on November 20, 2026, exclusively on Netflix . The series will be available to international viewers, including those in India, through the platform. 
 With a cross-border murder mystery, an unusual detective partnership, and a director experienced in crime storytelling, the series has several ingredients that thriller fans will appreciate. 
 Now the big question is whether Kim Seok and Inose can put aside their differences long enough to uncover the truth. 
 Are you planning to watch The Blue Road for Son Suk-ku, or does its Korean-Japanese detective storyline make you curious about the series?
